definitions.explanation: A beverage made from tea leaves. In Japanese, {茶|ちゃ} typically refers to Japanese green tea by default, though it can refer to tea in general.
The color brown, named after the color of tea. Used in compound words like {茶色|ちゃいろ} (brown color).

examples.japanese: {茶|ちゃ}を{一杯|いっぱい}{飲|の}みませんか。
examples.english: Would you like to have a cup of tea?

examples.japanese: {茶色|ちゃいろ}の{鞄|かばん}が{欲|ほ}しい。
{日本|にほん}では{食事|しょくじ}の{後|あと}にお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}む{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: In Japan, there's a custom of drinking tea after meals.

notes:
USAGE: The polite form お{茶|ちゃ} is more commonly used in everyday speech. Without any modifier, {茶|ちゃ}/お{茶|ちゃ} typically means Japanese green tea ({緑茶|りょくちゃ}).

TYPES OF TEA:
・{緑茶|りょくちゃ} (green tea)
・{紅茶|こうちゃ} (black tea)
・{麦茶|むぎちゃ} (barley tea)
・{抹茶|まっちゃ} (matcha, powdered green tea)
・ウーロン{茶|ちゃ} (oolong tea)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・お{茶|ちゃ}を{入|い}れる (to make/brew tea)
・お{茶|ちゃ}を{出|だ}す (to serve tea)
・{茶道|さどう}/{茶|ちゃ}の{湯|ゆ} (tea ceremony)

IDIOM: {茶|ちゃ}を{濁|にご}す means 'to evade the issue' or 'to gloss over something'.
